Commentary.Commentary: The Sri Lankans could not capitalize on the start they got as they were totally put on the back seat by some sensational batting. Sandakan was the pick of the bowlers but he was unlucky as they dropped a couple of catches off his bowling. They had to pay big for their bad fielding as both du Plessis and Miller went on to score tons after being given lives. Everyone bowled well but in phases and consistency was lacking there. Can the visitors pull off something special with the bat when they come out to chase? Join us in a while for it.

Beautiful display of batting by South Africa, after getting off to a relatively bad start. They have managed to impose a total just above 300, all thanks to some sensational batting performances by Faf du Plessis and David Miller. They both stuck it out in the middle as the Islanders had wrapped up their top order for less than 80 runs. They both raced away to their respective hundreds as they kept the score ticking at a brisk pace after they lost Duminy. du Plessis departed soon after his century but Miller stayed till the end. Chris Morris gave him a brief support in the middle but fell prey to Lakmal.

FOUR! Too full outside off, Miller gets down on it and manages to squeeze it over backward point for a boundary. The fielder leaps to catch that one but cannot stop it. That's a superb finish from Miller. SOUTH AFRICA END WITH 307/6 ON BOARD!

He could have been lucky since Lakmal had not picked it early but recovered well to dive to his left and grab it inches off the ground. What a way to get out. Cricket, a game of glorious uncertainties for a reason.

On a length outside off, Amla shuffles across a touch and defends it.
On a length on the stumps, de Kock tucks it through backward square leg for a single.
Quinton gets across a touch and looks to work it through mid-wicket but finds the fielder.
Hurls it on a length on the pads, de Kock fails to work it off his pads as the ball rolls towards the off side after contact.
Length ball outside off, Amla stays back and defends it.

FOUR! Dropped! Full outside off, Amla just drives it back down the wicket but in the air. The bowler has a second to react to it, going to his left to catch that one and he misses it. The ball races away to the fence.
Slants this on the stumps, Amla nudges it towards square leg but not for any run.
De kock tucks this one towards mid-wicket for a single.
On a touch short length outside off, dabbed towards backward point from de Kock.
Quinton de Kock looks to work this one through mid-wicket but ends up pushing it back down the wicket at the last moment.
Suranga Lakmal to bowl from the other end with the second new ball.
Length ball outside off, Amla is happy to shoulders his arms to it.
FOUR! A much better shot and results tells you the same! A back of a length delivery outside off, Amla is confident enough this time and punches it through covers for a superb boundary.
A tad short outside off, Amla punches it through the gap between cover and cover-point for a couple of runs to get off the mark.
Brings this one in from outside off, Amla stays back and defends it off his back foot.
Full outside off, swings away a touch, Amla lets it go through watchfully.
Starts off with a length ball outside off, left alone by Amla.
Game time! The players are out in the middle. The two South African openers Quinton de Kock and Hashim Amla are out to bat. Sri Lanka begin with Nuwan Kulasekara. Here we go...
South Africa XI - Quinton de Kock (wk), Hashim Amla, Faf du Plessis, AB de Villiers (c), Jean-Paul Duminy, David Miller, Chris Morris, Wayne Parnell, Andile Phehlukwayo, Kagiso Rabada, Imran Tahir.

Sri Lanka XI - Niroshan Dickwella, Kusal Mendis, Dinesh Chandimal (wk), Upul Tharanga (c), Dhananjaya de Silva, Chaturanga de Silva, Sachith Pathirana, Asela Gunaratne, Nuwan Kulasekara, Suranga Lakmal, Lakshan Sandakan.

TOSS - Sri Lanka win the toss and elect to bowl first. A couple of changes for them - Sachith Pathirana and Chaturanga de Silva come in for Jeffrey Vandersay, Sandun Weerakkody. South Africa are unchanged from the previous game.

The Sri Lankan batsmen have not found a way to counter the early swing with the new ball despite having spent over a month in the country. It was Angelo Mathews and Seekkuge Prasanna's brilliance that got them over the line in T20Is but things went down again in the first ODI. Upul Tharanga will aim to lead from the front and hope that his players can step up as they aim to stay alive in the series and not play catch up so early.

Hello everyone and welcome to the coverage of the second ODI between South Africa and Sri Lanka at the Kingsmead, Durban. The hosts had a superb first game where they outplayed the visitors to take a 1-0 lead. It was once again the bowlers who did the damage for the visitors as Wayne Parnell and Imran Tahir ran through their batting line-up. The top order for the hosts then completed the chase as clinically as they could. On a faster pitch in Durban, one expects things to not change much but expects a bit more fight from the Lankans at least.
